nodes.name: Ni foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: Ni foam was firstly cleaned by immersing in 3 M HCl for 30 min to remove the oxide layer. After that, the Ni foam was washed with DI water and dried in oven for several hours.

nodes.name: NiFe-LDH electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: NiFe-LDH was fabricated by an electrodeposition technique with a three-electrode measurement system with Ni foam (working), titanium foil (counter), and Ag/AgCl saturated KCl (reference) electrodes. Firstly, 0.1 mol NiCl₂·6H₂O and 0.1 mol FeCl₃ were dissolved into 100 mL DI water and stirred for 10 min to form the homogenous electrolyte solution (1 M NiCl₂ and 1 M FeCl₃). The electrodeposition was performed by a constant voltage technique at -1.0 V (versus Ag/AgCl saturated KCl) for 2.5 min under argon atmosphere. Finally, single-phase NiFe-LDH was carefully washed and dried at 90°C for 2 h.

nodes.name: Ni(OH)₂ electrodeposition on NiFe-LDH
nodes.procedure: To prepare NiFe-LDH/Ni(OH)₂ composite, as-fabricated NiFe-LDH/Ni foam was used as the working electrode in the second run of electrodeposition in 1 M NiCl₂ solution. After applying the potential of -1.0 V (vs Ag/AgCl) for 0.5 min, Ni(OH)₂ nanoparticle was successfully electrodeposited on the surface of NiFe-LDH. The NiFe-LDH/Ni(OH)₂ composite was then washed with ethanol and dried in oven at 70°C.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1a display the scanning electron microscope images of NiFe-LDH with vertically aligned nanosheet. The average thickness of that nanosheet structure was 33±8 nm. The morphology of Ni(OH)₂ in Fig. 1c is rough thin film ... After electrodepositing Ni(OH)₂, the surface of NiFe-LDH was much rougher ... The thickness of NiFe-LDH/Ni(OH)₂ composite was about 45±7 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH shows crystalline peaks at 2θ = 11.53°, 23.28°, 34.56°, and 39.01° corresponding to (003), (006), (012), and (015) planes (JCPDS No. 51-0463). Ni(OH)₂ is amorphous with no additional peaks. NiFe-LDH/Ni(OH)₂ shows similar pattern to NiFe-LDH but with lower intensity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction pattern of NiFe-LDH showed four peaks at 2θ = 11.53°, 23.28°, 34.56°, and 39.01° with crystal planes of (003), (006), (012), and (015), respectively ... X-ray diffraction of Ni(OH)₂ nanoparticle was similar to carbon cloth (substrate) without any additional peak, indicating its amorphous behavior.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH shows peaks at 472 and 556 cm⁻¹. Ni(OH)₂ shows broad peak at 475 cm⁻¹ confirming amorphous structure. NiFe-LDH/Ni(OH)₂ spectrum similar to Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy of NiFe-LDH clearly appears at 472 and 556 cm⁻¹ ... The broad and low-intensity peak of Ni(OH)₂ at 475 cm⁻¹ in the Raman spectrum also confirms its amorphous structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH: Ni 2p₃/₂ 856.4 eV, Ni 2p₁/₂ 874.0 eV (Ni²⁺); Fe 2p₃/₂ 711.9 eV, Fe 2p₁/₂ 725.0 eV (Fe³⁺); O 1s peaks at 531.16 eV (OH) and 533.27 eV (H₂O). NiFe-LDH/Ni(OH)₂: Ni peaks shift -0.6 eV to 855.8/873.4 eV; Fe signals weaker; Fe⁰ at 706.1 eV; O 1s at 528.51 eV (lattice) and 531.16 eV (OH).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The binding energies of Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ in NiFe-LDH located at 856.4 and 874.0 eV ... For NiFe-LDH/Ni(OH)₂ composite layer, the binding energies of nickel slightly shift about of 0.6 eV ... Two obvious peaks of Fe in NiFe-LDH are located at 725.0 eV and 711.9 eV ... The peak of metal iron (Fe⁰) is observable only for composite catalyst with binding energy of 706.1 eV ... The peaks which are located at binding energies of 531.16 and 533.27 eV are attributed to hydroxide oxygen (OH) and chemisorbed oxygen (H₂O)
